text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egypt invades direct investment market with huge economic and national projects. Prime Minister Ganzouri's talks in Abu Dhabi dealt with ways to boost economic cooperation with the United Arab Emirates.
- Mubarak to visti Germany on May 23 to discuss regional affairs and bilateral relations.
- Agriculture Minister Youssef Wali tells political club of National Democratic Party that wheat and cotton fields are in good condition.

- Wali tells conference on future of investment and agricultural development that Egypt would be self-sufficient in agricultural products by the year 2017; says that development outside of the Nile Valley led to discovery of 35 large oil fields and that there are 10 new oil agreements that govern projects in Upper Egypt and the Red Sea that will encourage investment.
- U.S. ambassador's study says cooperation with Egypt is essential for facing problems of peace and that Mubarak's policies enjoy wide support in the region.
- Central Bank governor says international financial standards are to be applied to banks in Egypt in July.
- Policeman martyred and six wounded in clash with terrorists in southern Egypt.
- Cabinet to review on Thursday the political and economic situation and the draft budget. Spending expected to total 83 billion pounds.
- Defence minister says, ahead of celebrations of Sinai Liberation Day, that battle to take Sinai back from Israel was no less important than the victory in October 1973.
- Finance minister says government is committed to reducing burden on citizens and that food subsidies would continue.
